GOOGLE ANTIGRAVITY: The End of the Copilot? The Future of Programming with AI Agents

The video analyzes the release of Google Antigravity, an experimental platform that proposes to move the AI from copilot to agent. Explains the agent-first model, verifiable artifacts and Manager Surface, the mixed reception of the launch and the new role of those who develop: set goals, review plans and guide agents.

Published in 19 November 2025 · 7 min 32 s

  • Agentic engineering
  • AI tools

Open on YouTube

The video and the transcript are in Portuguese. The minutes between brackets lead to the stretch of the video.

In this article

  1. From copilot to agent
  2. Google Antigravity
  3. Artifacts and Manager Surface
  4. The launch
  5. The new role of those who develop
  6. Frequently Asked Questions

From copilot to agent

The video is one of the biggest turns in software development: the passage of tools that help program for AI agents that program alone. A Google platform can be the protagonist 00:00.

Today the AI is copilot: suggests code and points errors. What if she took the wheel, getting missions instead of orders? 00:21

The script: where the AI is packing today, Antigravity, change to agents, working in practice, launching and what this means for the future 00:41.

The current tools complete code, hunt bugs and write entire functions, but the one with the ultimate responsibility is always the person 01:03. Today's AI is reactive: waits for command, and the person defines architecture, manages the project and validates the result 01:26.

Google Antigravity

Google Antigravity was announced as an experimental platform, aiming to go beyond the copilot: an AI that acts and takes initiative 01:46.

The key expression is agent-first. It's not an editor with a chatbot next door: the platform revolves around the agent, and the editor becomes just one of his tools. 01:46.

Google built Antigravity on VS Code 02:08. It comes with Gemini, but also runs models of Anthropic and OpenAI 02:30.

The change is abstraction: instead of "eswrite a function to sort a list", the order becomes "crie a component that displays data from an API and allows you to sort" 02:30. Whoever develops comes out of the code trench line by line and focuses on what needs to be done; how it becomes agent problem 02:51.

The agent cycle 03:13:

1. Understands the goal 03:13. 2. Plans the tasks, breaking the problem into parts 03:13. 3. Write code, test and correct mistakes themselves 03:13. 4. Check if the delivery works. 03:35.

Artifacts and Manager Surface

The biggest challenge of an autonomous agent is trust: how to know what he did? 03:55 Antigravity's response is artifacts, clear and verifiable progress reports, rather than indecipherable logs. 03:55.

Examples of artifacts 03:55:

  • The list of tasks the agent plans to perform 04:17.
  • The detailed implementation plan 04:17.
  • Screenshots and agent recordings testing the application in the browser 04:17.

The second innovation is Manager Surface, a control tower to launch and orchestrate several agents in parallel, as a team 04:37.

The most radical idea: the agent stops living inside the editor. It is the central entity, and editor, terminal and browser are tools that it uses 04:57.

The launch

According to the video, the initial reception was mixed 04:57. Many people have faced log-in errors, crashes and exhausted API quotas after a single task 05:18.

Some users were successful and compared Antigravity well to other agency tools 05:38. But for each good report, there were others of people trapped in installation loops. 05:59.

The criticisms, in short 05:59:

  • Technical problems of a hasty launch 05:59.
  • The skepticism with Google's history of abandoning products 05:59.
  • The perception that the idea was not so new 06:19.
  • Concerns with usage quotas and privacy 06:19.

The new role of those who develop

Whatever the fate of Antigravity, it signals where development is headed. 06:19. The work of those who do it does not disappear: it rises. The main skill is to define clear goals, review architecture plans and guide the agent with feedback 06:41.

The person ceases to be a builder and becomes an architect and project manager, overseeing a team of agents 07:01. The final question: if agents have seen the developers, what does the human developer become? 07:01

Frequently Asked Questions

What does agent-first mean?

That the platform revolves around the AI agent, and the editor, the terminal and the browser are tools that it uses 01:46.

What are the Antigravity artifacts?

About the video

* ==References== The End of the Copilot? The Future of Programming with AI Agents**

Artificial Intelligence is about to change software development forever!

In this video, we do an in-depth analysis of **Google Antigravity**, the platform that promises to transform the AI from a simple "copilot" to an autonomous "agente", capable of running end-to-end projects.

If you are a developer, technology enthusiast or curious about the future of programming, this content is essential to understanding the next great revolution.

* ♪ What are you gonna find out ♪

* ** The Copilot Transition to Agent:** Why reactive AI is no longer sufficient and how Antigravity proposes a "agent-first" model.
* ** Antigravity Mechanics:** Understand how the platform uses "Artefatos" (verifiable deliverables) and a "Manager Surface" to orchestrate the work of multiple AI agents.
* **Hype vs. Reality:** We analyzed the tool's revolutionary potential and the practical challenges of its initial release (log-in errors, API quotas, etc.).
* ** The New Developer Role:** Find out why the programmer's future is not to be an executor, but an architect and strategist, setting goals and providing feedback for the AI.

The future of the code is autonomous. Watch now and prepare for the era of handless software development!
